solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Repeat of Crécy? Clearly, in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A historian wonders whether some later battle was clearly a rerun of Crécy, the 1346 English victory in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something again, or process waste for reuse, is to put it through another round; both senses fit a noun-like 'repeat' used as a verb.

clue.text: Person taking off after touching farm machinery

indicators.note: after says the mimic comes after the word for touching

parts.note: re means about, concerning
an aper is a mimic, one taking someone off

explanation.surface: A person takes off after making contact with farm machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking off' suggests leaving; here it means impersonating.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that cuts grain at harvest is a piece of farm equipment.

clue.text: Nick takes short trip

parts.note: to cop is to take or catch
a hop is a short journey

explanation.surface: Someone named Nick goes on a quick outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang for a police station, and also for stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for a police station, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Girl on small boat when Jack's boarded vessel for Bordeaux

indicators.note: on says the girl sits above the boat in this down entry

parts.note: Clare is a girl's name

indicators.note: boarded says the jack gets on to the small boat, inside it

parts.note: a tug is a small boat
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A girl on a tug when Jack has come aboard pours from a decanter of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' suggests a sailor; it is the card J.
explanation.definitionFit: A jug for red Bordeaux wine, known in Britain as claret; also the Open golf trophy.

clue.text: Mature, upwardly mobile daughter, dated brother

indicators.note: upwardly mobile says the word moves upward, read bottom to top in this down entry

parts.note: to mature is to age

explanation.surface: A mature, socially climbing daughter went out with a brother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brother' is the exclamation, as in 'Oh brother!', and 'dated' says the oath is old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned exclamation of surprise, like 'Oh brother!' in modern speech.

clue.text: Former champion from China, these days at home

parts.note: china plate is cockney rhyming slang for mate, so china means a pal
AD, anno domini, the present era
at home means in

explanation.surface: A one-time title holder from China is now living at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is rhyming slang: china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight of Charlemagne's court, and so a chivalrous champion of a cause, from long ago.

clue.text: Coastal regions provided one with cover when lifting felon

indicators.note: lifting says the cover is raised, read upwards in this down entry

parts.note: a cap is a cover
provided means if
I is the Roman numeral one
crim is slang for criminal

explanation.surface: A felon has been provided with protection when he was lifting goods.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed cap leads the entry though named after 'provided one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The lands bordering the great ocean are a collective term for its coastal regions.

clue.text: Fabric's length: an inch under

definitions.note: the definition is the fabric, with 's standing for is as the link

indicators.note: under says the island comes below the length in this down entry

parts.note: inch is a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.surface: The material's length is an inch short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inch' looks like a measurement; in Scotland an inch is an islet.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine twisted cotton thread used for stockings, and the cloth woven from it.

clue.text: Had snack prepared, leaving out cold dish

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters are rearranged
leaving out says the cold letter is dropped from the fodder

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, on taps

explanation.surface: Someone had a snack ready but left out a cold dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A Parsi curry of meat cooked with lentils, a dish on Indian restaurant menus.

clue.text: Put up with bird gatecrashing do perhaps

indicators.note: gatecrashing says the bird gets inside the do

parts.note: do is a note of the sol-fa scale
mina is a variant spelling of myna, an Asian starling

explanation.surface: Someone has to put up with a bird crashing a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' suggests a party; it is the note.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up a candidate is to propose them for election.

clue.text: Attendance record, perhaps, one might want to keep up

definitions.meaning: a player's record of games turned out for, counted as caps or showings

definitions.text: one might want to keep up
definitions.meaning: to keep up a show of normality is the set phrase, so this is the thing kept up

explanation.surface: A record of attendance is something a person might want to maintain.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsman's tally of games played is counted in showings; and the idiom 'keep up' takes this word to mean outward show.

clue.text: Prime strip of land?

definitions.meaning: to prime a bomb or weapon is to make it ready to fire
a narrow projection of land into the sea, like a limb

explanation.surface: Is the finest strip of land on offer?
explanation.definitionFit: Priming a device and readying a weapon are the same act; and a narrow inlet or headland is called by the limb's name.

clue.text: Like cave, maybe, or garden in city, close to cemetery

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
to garden is to hoe

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word cemetery

explanation.surface: Something is like a cave, or like a garden in the city near a cemetery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' tempts a solver to put the garden inside the city, but the letters only fit side by side; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cave resounds, giving back sounds, so a reverberant place is described this way.

clue.text: Soothing stuff from peace-keepers following confrontation on pitch

indicators.note: following says the peace-keepers come after the confrontation

parts.note: in football, afters is the scuffle that follows a foul
UN, the United Nations, which sends peace-keeping forces

explanation.surface: A soothing balm is supplied by peace-keepers after a fight on a football pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is British football slang for a bout of retaliation after a tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion applied to skin after sunbathing calms burnt skin, so it is soothing stuff.

clue.text: What's invested intelligently after small, momentary lapses

indicators.note: after says the anagram comes after the small letter
lapses means slips or errors, so the letters of momentary fall into a new order

explanation.surface: After brief momentary lapses, one wonders what's being invested wisely.
explanation.definitionFit: Funds placed by shrewd, well-informed investors are what is put in by those in the know.

clue.text: Version of game giving coloured jacket primacy?

indicators.note: coloured means altered or distorted, so the letters of jacket primacy are rearranged

explanation.surface: A form of the sport puts its coloured kit first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coloured' also describes the kit: one-day cricket is played in coloured clothing, mocked as pyjamas, so the clue half-defines itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Limited-overs cricket, played in coloured kit rather than whites, is a variety of the game.

clue.text: E-learning worked, mainly

indicators.note: worked means manipulated or wrought, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Online learning has mostly been a success.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means for the most part, on the whole, so largely.

clue.text: Objections raised, presumably not made difficult

indicators.note: raised says the word goes upward, read bottom to top in this down entry

parts.note: buts are objections, as in no ifs or buts
a person is born rather than made, as in a born leader

explanation.surface: Objections are raised that something was not made difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstinate person refuses to give way, so is hard to deal with.

clue.text: Firing agent giving grass to actor's horse

indicators.note: to says the grass is attached on after the horse

parts.note: Trigger was the horse of cowboy actor Roy Rogers
to grass is to inform on, to point the finger

explanation.surface: Someone sacks an agent for feeding grass to an actor's horse.
explanation.walkthrough: To grass, British slang, is to inform to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: The digit that squeezes a gun's release does the shooting, so it is the agent of firing.

clue.text: What waiter might use to cover in sugar and cream

parts.note: to ice a cake is to cover it in sugar
the cream is the pick, the best

explanation.surface: A waiter might use something to cover a dessert in sugar and cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waiter' is a mountaineer waiting on a frozen ledge, or a bartender chipping ice, not a restaurant server.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiked tool for breaking frozen water, which a bar waiter chips cubes with.

clue.text: Defensive structure in the Suffolk area?

parts.note: the Suffolk is a breed of sheep, so a ram
a part is an area or region

explanation.surface: Is there a defensive structure in the Suffolk area?
explanation.walkthrough: Suffolk is an English county, but here it is the sheep breed of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad defensive wall or embankment around a fort is a protective structure.

clue.text: Name that's good for a female

parts.note: for a female means belonging to a lady, the possessive

explanation.surface: A name that suits a woman well.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so an example of a name.

clue.text: Necessity for pub social event: piano in rear

parts.note: a bee is a gathering, like a sewing bee

indicators.note: in says the piano goes inside the rear

parts.note: the rear is the rump
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A pub needs a social night, with a piano at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub cannot serve draught ale without the handle-operated device that draws it from the cellar.

clue.text: Happy news about dad is handled inappropriately

parts.note: pa is dad
news of a marriage is happy news, and wed means married

explanation.surface: Happy news about dad is dealt with badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The happy news about dad is that he is wed: PA WED.
explanation.definitionFit: To paw someone is to touch or grope them clumsily or improperly.

clue.text: Hides out of panic, small creature

indicators.note: the skins (hides) are taken off each word, leaving the inner letters of panic and small

explanation.surface: A small creature hides, out of panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hides' looks like a verb of concealment; read as skins, it removes the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Any living beast is a creature; the two words are close synonyms.

clue.text: States field officer should cut unexplained overheads?

indicators.note: cut says the officer slices into the States

parts.note: US is the United States

explanation.surface: The States says a field officer should cut its unexplained overhead costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overheads' suggests business costs; here it means things flying overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Unidentified flying objects are lights in the sky nobody has explained.

clue.text: Passed on one's charm

parts.note: OB, short for obiit, he died, as on tombstones
one is I, with the 's as is

explanation.surface: Someone passed on their charm to the next generation.
explanation.walkthrough: OB. is the Latin abbreviation for 'died' used in records.
explanation.definitionFit: A West African word for sorcery, also used of a fetish or amulet, which is a charm.

clue.text: Extension serving part of hospital, one of fifteen

parts.note: a wing is an extension to a building
serving means for, in favour of
a ward is a hospital section

explanation.surface: A hospital extension serves one of its departments.
explanation.walkthrough: A rugby union team has fifteen players.
explanation.definitionFit: A flanker position in the rugby union scrum, one player in a side of fifteen.

clue.text: Parasite, large, in denial, plainly

indicators.note: in says the parasite and large go into the denial

parts.note: nay is a refusal
a ked is a sheep tick, a parasite

explanation.surface: A large parasite is plainly in denial.
explanation.definitionFit: Done without disguise or covering, so openly and without adornment.

clue.text: Acknowledges characters involved in a tussle

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the characters of a tussle are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone acknowledges the people caught up in a scuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Greeting someone with a raised hand recognises their presence, a gesture of acknowledgement.
